newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jospin says opposes France's full return to NATO.
newsitem.headline: Jospin says opposes France's full return to NATO.

text.p: Socialist opposition leader Lionel Jospin said on Sunday he would oppose Gaullist President Jacques Chirac's move to bring France back into NATO's military wing if a forthcoming parliamentary election took him to power.
Jospin said Chirac's initiative could be thwarted as France was not getting the concessions it asked for in return, including the transfer of NATO's southern command to a European officer.
"I believe I heard it said that, if we could not obtain the concessions the move would be aborted," he told France 3 television in an interview.
"If it were...it would suit me fully," he said.
Washington has rejected relinquishing the Naples-based southern command which includes control over the U.S. Mediterranean Sixth Fleet.

Jospin said he had never agreed to the government's move, and he was surprised that it was made by a disciple of the late General Charles de Gaulle who had taken France out of the Atlantic alliance's military organisation.
Opinion polls released at the weekend said Chirac's centre-right coalition's lead was slipping a week ahead of the first round of the May 25-June 1 election to the National Assembly.
